title: Building an Agentic Video Editor for Mass Consumer — Ekaterina Deyneka, Reelful
talk_summary: Ekaterina Deyneka describes Reelful, an agentic video editor that runs an agent with skills inside a remote sandbox to produce Remotion (video-as-React-code) compositions from user media plus a prompt. The pipeline is media understanding/transcription, a user-approved creative plan, sandboxed agent execution with craft skills, code-based composition, and a verification layer that makes the agent re-iterate on defects.

takeaways.technique: Deterministic verification layer that forces agent re-iteration
takeaways.what_they_do: After the agent produces a composition, a separate verification layer checks that it is clean, well-defined, and renderable; on failure the agent re-iterates on the composition before delivery.
The agent first produces a creative plan from media understanding and the user approves or regenerates it before any sandbox is spun up and editing begins.

takeaways.technique: Craft encoded as reusable skills in the sandbox
takeaways.what_they_do: The agent runs with packaged skills encoding domain taste and rules (cut rules for best moments, font pairs, how to generate b-rolls) rather than relying on ad-hoc prompting.

takeaways.technique: Ephemeral remote sandbox per approved job
takeaways.what_they_do: Execution happens in a remote machine spun up per approved plan, isolating the agent's tools and skills from the host; the same pattern is used for both app-builder and video-editor agents.

takeaways.technique: Represent artifacts as code the agent can write and validate
takeaways.what_they_do: They use Remotion so the video composition is React code, exploiting that agents are strong at writing code, and the verification layer can check the code artifact.
takeaways.evidence_quote: agents are really good at writing code and therefore we can use them to create videos with this remotion framework
